standard.note: Public Act 19-4 indexed Connecticut to the federal Employment Cost Index from 2024; $16.35 in 2025, $16.94 in 2026.

tipped.note: Connecticut runs TWO tipped rates, split by occupation rather than by employer: hotel and restaurant staff at a $6.38 cash wage, bartenders at $8.23. Both are frozen dollar figures, so every ECI increase lands entirely on the tip credit.

variants.label: Bartender cash wage
variants.test: An employee who customarily and regularly receives tips while working as a bartender.
variants.note: CORRECTED 2026-11-06: the bartender CASH wage is $8.23 and the tip credit is the rest of the minimum wage ($8.71 at $16.94); the file had the two reversed ($8.71 cash, $8.23 credit). Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-60 sets $8.23 as the employer's share for bartenders who customarily receive gratuities, and the Department of Labor's tip statement (effective 2026-01-01) reads: 'As a bartender, I have received gratuities of at least 51.42% of the minimum wage of $16.94 per hour (equaling at least $8.71 per hour)... My guaranteed wage is $8.23 per hour in 2026.'
